title: Dyson Spheres and Kardashev Scale Megastructures
executive_summary: A Dyson sphere is a hypothetical megastructure that completely encompasses a star to capture a large percentage of its solar power output, proposed by physicist Freeman Dyson in 1960.
image_caption: Illustration of a Dyson Swarm of solar-harvesting collectors orbiting a star.

key_sections.title: Dyson Swarms vs Solid Shells
key_sections.content: Rather than an impossible rigid shell, Dyson proposed a 'Dyson Swarm' consisting of millions of independent solar collector satellites orbiting in dense shells around a star.

key_sections.title: The Kardashev Scale (Types I, II, III)
key_sections.content: Nikolai Kardashev classified civilizations by energy consumption: Type I (planetary energy), Type II (total stellar power of one star), and Type III (total galaxy energy output).

key_sections.title: Infrared Waste Heat Signatures
key_sections.content: Search for Extraterrestrial Technology (SETT) projects look for Dyson spheres by scanning the sky for stars emitting excessive mid-infrared waste heat with reduced optical brightness.
